new_statements.quote: While vowel length is contrastive in all Greater Ok languages except Mian and Oksapmin, the distinction between long and short vowels is lacking in Greater Awyu. While Mountain Ok languages are described as tonal (Telefol, Tifal, Mian), in Lowland Ok and Greater Awyu languages it is not the tone contour but lexical stress that seems to be distinctive. [p. 18:] Both languages [Muyu and Mandobo] have distinctive lexical stress, as is true for all other Awyu-Dumut languages and some other Ok languages.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File held by the project (HAL hal-03950196 deposit, 4.5 MB) plus A's 300-dpi scanned extract of pp. 3, 6, 19. Both quoted sentences are verbatim in the extract: p. 2 'While Mountain Ok languages are described as tonal (Telefol, Tifal, Mian), in Lowland Ok and Greater Awyu languages it is not the tone contour but lexical stress that seems to be distinctive.' and p. 18 'Both languages have distinctive lexical stress, as is true for all other Awyu-Dumut languages and some other Ok languages.' (A spliced the two with a '[p. 18:]' marker, hence minor-differences). a full-text search for stress/accent the full extracted text for Iwur|Morop|Murop|Iwoer|Dintere: zero hits; p. 5 defines Lowland Ok a…
new_statements.relation_note: Only the two family-level sentences quoted; phoneme-inventory sizes, vowel length contrast in Greater Ok; nothing specific to Iwur.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level claim only: in Lowland Ok (the subgroup Iwur is tentatively assigned to) lexical stress, not tone, is said to be distinctive (i.e. contrastive/lexical stress, no tone); no stress position is given and Iwur is not among the languages examined.
new_statements.exceptions: Mountain Ok languages (Telefol, Tifal, Mian) are tonal instead; p. 18 weakens the Ok half of the claim to 'some other Ok languages'.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog attaches this paper to iwur1240, but Iwur/Morop is never named in it: Lowland Ok is treated as 'Ngalum, Kati [Muyu], Ninggerum, and Yonggom, plus some languages not further considered here' (p. 5). The prosody remark is a family-level generalisation for 'Lowland Ok and Greater Awyu languages', resting on Muyu/Yonggom/Awyu-Dumut descriptions; it covers Iwur only by classification (Iwur's Lowland Ok membership is itself tentative per Healey 1964 and Voorhoeve 1975). Not first-hand Iwur data.
